title: Normalized diagonal orientation on etale charts at arbitrary finite coefficient stages
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient stage $\Lambda=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, $n\geq1$, in [def-pur-conventions], with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$ and any finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a smooth separated finite-type morphism of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ between finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Put $\omega_f=Rf^!\Lambda_Y$ using [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and let $\vartheta_f:\omega_f\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_X(d)[2d]$ be the specified diagonal orientation [thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object, def-coefficient-twists-detailed].

Let $V\subseteq Y$ and $U\subseteq f^{-1}V$ be affine open subschemes, put $h=f|_U:U\to V$, and write $j:U\hookrightarrow X$. For $W_h=U\times_VU$ with first projection $p_h$ and diagonal $\Delta_h$, set $C_h=L\Delta_h^*\omega_{p_h}$ [def-pur-section-invariant]. Let $N_h=N_{\Delta_h/W_h}$ be the normal bundle [def-pur-normal-bundle], $N_h\cong T_{U/V}$ [lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion], $\pi_h:N_h\to U$ and $0_h:U\to N_h$ its zero section [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section]. Let $\alpha_h:C_h\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_h$ be [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change], $\delta_h:C_h\xrightarrow{\sim}C(\pi_h,0_h)$ the uniquely normalized comparison [thm-pur-dnc-invariance], and $\beta_h:C(\pi_h,0_h)\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_U(d)[2d]$ the restriction to $0_h$ of [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity]. Under the canonical open-restriction comparison $Lj^*\omega_f\cong\omega_h$,
$$Lj^*\vartheta_f=\vartheta_h=\beta_h\circ\delta_h\circ\alpha_h^{-1}.$$
These assemblies commute with further restriction of $U,V$.

If $h$ has an etale coordinate morphism $u:U\to\mathbf A^d_V$ [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-sbc-affine-space], the coordinate differences on the two factors of $W_h$ give etale coordinates near $\Delta_h$ carrying $(p_h,\Delta_h)$ to the standard zero-section pair $(\mathbf A^d_U\to U,0)$ and identify $N_h$ with $\mathcal O_U^d$. The comparison is made through the actual coordinate data: the centred-coordinate theorem supplies an open neighbourhood $O$ of $\Delta_h$ in $W_h$ and a section $s:U\to O$ with $\iota_O\circ s=\Delta_h$, for which $O\to\mathbf A^d_U$ given by the coordinate differences is etale and the zero-section square is Cartesian. Write $D_d=C(\mathbf A^d_U\to U,0)$. The source-coordinate isomorphism $c_{\mathrm{src}}:C_h\xrightarrow{\sim}D_d$ is the open restriction to $O$ followed by the inverse etale restriction from the standard pair, using the exceptional-adjunction comparisons and the Cartesian zero square. Independently, the canonical symmetric-algebra map from the conormal piece $\mathcal I_{\Delta_h}/\mathcal I_{\Delta_h}^2$ to the associated graded algebra [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra-basic, lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra], together with the homogeneous-normalized Rees comparison [def-pur-rees-cone-normalization, lem-pur-rees-cone-normalized-existence], identifies the actual normal cone with the symmetric total space of that conormal module, preserving projection and zero section. The degree-one identification $[y(a)-x(a)]\mapsto da$ identifies the conormal module with $\Omega_{U/V}$; the pulled-back coordinate differentials give its ordered free frame [lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion]. Thus this actual normal-bundle comparison identifies $N_h$ with $\mathcal O_U^d$, with its zero section identified with the standard zero section. Let $c_N:C(\pi_h,0_h)\xrightarrow{\sim}D_d$ be the section-invariant comparison induced by this normal-bundle coordinate map. Then $c_N\circ\delta_h\circ c_{\mathrm{src}}^{-1}=1_{D_d}$ and $\beta_h$ is the zero-section restriction of the rank-$d$ vector-bundle comparison. The formula includes $d=0$, where the centred neighbourhood, standard section comparison, differential frame, and rank-zero bundle comparison are the corresponding identity data.

In these coordinates let $P_d:\mathbf A^d_V\to V$ and let $\Gamma_{P_d,\Lambda}:\Lambda_{\mathbf A^d_V}(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{P_d}$ be the ordered affine comparison [def-pur-affine-space-comparison], extended to every $n\geq1$ exactly as specified in [lem-pur-projection-purity-agreement]. Let $\epsilon_u:\omega_h=R(P_du)^!\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}Lu^*\omega_{P_d}$ be exceptional composition [pur9-def-upper-shriek-composition] followed by the canonical etale identification $Ru^!=Lu^*$. Then the same local assembly satisfies
$$\vartheta_h=Lu^*(\Gamma_{P_d,\Lambda}^{-1})\circ\epsilon_u.$$
Thus its coordinate and normal-bundle comparisons are the ones defined by the exceptional adjunctions, rather than arbitrary trivializations. If $B$ is affine, $P_r:\mathbf A^r_B\to B$, and $z_r$ is its zero section, write $D_r=Lz_r^*\omega_{P_r}$. The standard zero-section vector-bundle orientation $b_r:D_r\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_B(r)[2r]$ in the preceding normalization is precisely $Lz_r^*(\Gamma_{P_r,\Lambda}^{-1})$, with the canonical twist restriction. All these identifications commute with further open restriction and etale changes of coordinate charts. This statement is for arbitrary finite $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and all $n\geq1$.

proof.text: Work over the affine chart V and put h=f|_U, W_h=U\times_VU, with first projection p_h and diagonal Delta_h. The section invariant is C_h=LDelta_h^*omega_{p_h}. The Cartesian square for p_h over h and the base-change comparison for the exceptional inverse image give the canonical isomorphism alpha_h:C_h~>omega_h. This is exactly the diagonal base-change comparison, since p_h\circ Delta_h=id_U.

source.place: Diagonal-dualizing-object proof Step 1; chart proof Step 3, source-map comparison

proof.text: The diagonal Delta_h is a regular closed immersion of codimension d and its normal bundle is canonically N_h~=T_{U/V}. Applying the normalized deformation-to-the-normal-cone theorem to the smooth section (p_h,Delta_h) gives the unique delta_h:C_h~>C(pi_h,0_h) which is the identity on the standard pair in etale coordinates. The fiber and coordinate descriptions of the DNC identify the two endpoint section invariants, so this comparison is compatible with restriction and base change. Use the centred smooth-section coordinates to obtain the regular conormal model. Fix its relative-Spec isomorphism by the canonical symmetric comparison and the normalized Rees identification on homogeneous ideal classes; no zero-preserving bundle automorphism is left unspecified.

source.place: Chart proof Steps 2–3, normal bundle and normalized DNC comparison

proof.text: Vector-bundle purity for pi_h, pulled back along the zero section, gives beta_h:C(pi_h,0_h)~>Lambda_U(d)[2d]. Its compatibility with base change and direct sums makes beta_h depend only on the actual normal bundle and its zero section, with the canonical Tate pullback. Therefore the three displayed arrows form the assembly beta_h circ delta_h circ alpha_h^{-1}.

By the definition of the specified diagonal orientation in the diagonal-dualizing-object theorem, the orientation on h is precisely beta_h circ delta_h circ alpha_h^{-1}. The same construction for f restricts along the open immersion j:U->X: exceptional composition, section-invariant pullback, the normalized DNC comparison, and vector-bundle purity all commute with this restriction. Hence under the canonical open-restriction comparison Lj^*omega_f~=omega_h one has Lj^*vartheta_f=vartheta_h.

source.place: Diagonal-dualizing-object proof Steps 1–2 and chart proof final restriction paragraph

proof.text: Assume now that u:U->A^d_V is etale. The product map on the two factors is etale by stability under base change. Near Delta_h, the coordinate differences of the two pullbacks of the standard coordinates cut out the diagonal; the resulting map W_h->A^d_U is etale and carries Delta_h to the zero section. Its differential identifies N_h with the trivial rank-d bundle O_U^d. The coordinate and DNC descriptions in the section-geometry lemma, together with the uniqueness clause of the DNC theorem, therefore identify delta_h with the identity comparison for the standard zero-section pair. This also covers d=0, when the pair is already the identity pair. On the centred neighbourhood O, define c_src by restricting C(p_h,Delta_h) to O and then inverting etale restriction from the standard zero pair; the Cartesian zero square fixes the section. Define c_N from the canonical conormal model and differential frame by the same normalized exceptional-adjunction restriction. The resulting equality is c_N delta_h c_src^{-1}=id on D_d, also for d=0.

source.place: Chart proof Steps 1–3 and the standard-pair normalization

proof.text: Under the same coordinate identification, beta_h is the pullback to the zero section of the rank-d vector-bundle comparison for O_U^d. Base-change compatibility of vector-bundle purity and the canonical pullback of Tate twists show that no frame-dependent scalar or sign is introduced. Thus the local assembly is the normalized standard zero-section orientation in the chosen coordinates.

source.place: Chart proof Step 4, vector-bundle integration and frame independence

proof.text: The ordered affine comparison Gamma_{P_d,Lambda} is extended to every n>=1 by projection-purity-agreement. In the current constructible composition definition take f=u, g=P_d, and L=Lambda_V in D^b_c(V,A). Both maps are separated finite type between affine finite-type k-schemes. The defining comparison c_{P_d,u,Lambda_V} is the conjugate of the compact-support composition isomorphism; def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate makes it invertible. Its evaluation is legitimate: K=R(P_du)^!Lambda_V is bounded constructible and has the etale-origin witness specified in pur9-def-upper-shriek-composition; compact support preserves the bounded-below etale-origin class. Compose c with the canonical etale identification Ru^!=Lu^* to obtain epsilon_u. Steps 2, 5 and 6 identify the diagonal, normalized DNC and zero-section arrows with the pullbacks of the corresponding arrows for P_d. Their composite is therefore Lu^*(vartheta_{P_d}) circ epsilon_u. Projection-purity-agreement at K=Lambda_V identifies vartheta_{P_d}=Gamma_{P_d,Lambda}^{-1}, giving the required formula for vartheta_h. For P_r over affine B, the same model agreement identifies its dualizing orientation with Gamma_{P_r,Lambda}^{-1}; pulling back along z_r gives b_r=Lz_r^*(Gamma_{P_r,Lambda}^{-1}) with canonical twist restriction.

source.place: Chart proof Step 4 and projection-purity-agreement normalization

proof.text: Further open restrictions and etale changes of chart pull back the same diagonal, normal-bundle and vector-bundle arrows (Steps 2, 5 and 6), so uniqueness of the normalized DNC comparison identifies the pulled-back DNC arrow with the new one. For the exceptional comparisons, thm-sf-comp-composition gives identity and associativity of alpha on bounded-below etale-origin inputs. Conjugation and mate pasting carry these equations to the comparisons c defined by pur9-def-upper-shriek-composition; all inputs here are the bounded constructible objects of Step 7. Thus the coordinate-adjunction expression is compatible with the same restrictions and chart changes. For d=0, the standard section pair is the identity pair, the normalized DNC map is the identity, and projection-purity-agreement gives Gamma_{P_0,Lambda}=1. The rank-zero zero-section pullback is also the identity. Hence every displayed formula has the claimed unit value.

statement_change.what: The coordinate clause asserted that δ_h was the identity under section-invariant and normal-bundle comparisons without stating the actual comparisons that determine those identifications. The source proof requires the centred etale neighbourhood and Cartesian zero square from the coordinate-difference construction, the canonical conormal normal-cone model with projection and zero-section preservation, and the normalized differential frame. The statement now records those data, including the rank-zero case, before asserting the identity. This repair defines both section-invariant coordinate maps as actual composites and states their conjugation equation; Lean identifier references in the mathematical statement are replaced by descriptions and owner-node citations. The conormal model is fixed by the relative-Spec symmetric comparison and normalized homogeneous Rees coordinates, preventing a zero-preserving automorphism from changing its frame.
